question.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Represents a Combination of Two Linear Transformations
question.problem:
Construct the matrix of the linear transformation that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- it rotates the vector by $\frac{5\pi }{4}$ radians clockwise about the origin, and then

- stretches the result by a stretch factor of $\frac{1}{6}$ parallel to the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation and let $Q$ be the matrix that represents the stretch. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\ Q & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6} & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $QP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}QP & =(\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}])(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{6\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 6 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
